name: Spark-X2.6-4B

lineage.how_derived: improved post-training of the Spark-X2.5-4B architecture (same architecture); a 1.7B sibling and a base model are also released

purpose: Compact general-purpose model for on-device agents: stronger coding, agentic, long-context, multilingual and reasoning ability than Spark-X2.5, with three thinking levels (none, low, high) (card).

license.name: Apache-2.0
license.notes: Apache License 2.0 text read in the repo LICENSE file: commercial use, modification and redistribution allowed with notice and patent grant.

architecture.kind: dense transformer, 36 layers, 3:1 sliding-window to full attention (custom code)
architecture.attention: sliding window layers plus a full-attention layer every 4th; 16 Q / 4 KV heads, head dim 256, headwise sigmoid output gate; hidden 2560

variants.notes: 6.3k downloads; vendor: reasoning effort high to low costs 4.0 average points and 37.3 percent of output length

pc-12gb.notes: 3.54 GB file fits the VRAM budget (9.6 GB) with room for KV

pc-16gb.notes: 3.54 GB file fits the VRAM budget (13.6 GB) with room for KV

pc-24gb.notes: 3.54 GB file fits the VRAM budget (21.6 GB) with room for KV

pc-32gb.notes: 3.54 GB file fits the VRAM budget (29.6 GB) with room for KV

mac-16-24gb.notes: 3.54 GB file against a GPU share of about 12 GB (KV cache not included)

mac-32gb.notes: 3.54 GB file against a GPU share of about 22 GB (KV cache not included)

mac-64gb+.notes: 3.54 GB file against a GPU share of about 52 GB (KV cache not included)

engine_support.notes: Official GGUF is published (so a llama.cpp path exists), but the architecture is custom (spark2_5); support level not verified.

strengths: 4B model with 1M context and a controllable thinking budget: high to low lowers the vendor's average score by 1.7 points and output length by 22 percent
weaknesses: benchmark charts are images only; no numbers were extractable, so no score is recorded here
soft.behavior: recommended sampling temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 0, thinking on by default in the example
soft.maturity: second release within about five weeks of Spark-X2.5; 35k downloads, 1.07k likes of the main repo, 882k of the official GGUF

tona_fit.reason: Small and cheap (3.5 GB Q4) but the vendor claim of matching 9B models rests on charts we could not read; at this size our users are better served by a measured Qwen3.5-4B or Gemma 4 E4B comparison before any offer. Useful as a draft or helper candidate.

open_questions: numbers behind the benchmark SVGs and independent results
